newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-DEION SANDERS RETURNS TO BASEBALL WITH REDS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-DEION SANDERS RETURNS TO BASEBALL WITH REDS.

text.p: Deion Sanders, who wants to add a World Series ring to his championship jewelry collection, will once again be a two-sport star after signing a contract to return to major league baseball with the Cincinnati Reds on Thursday.

Sanders, who sat out the 1996 baseball season to concentrate on playing football for the Dallas Cowboys, signed a one-year contract with the Reds with a mutual option year. Financial terms of the deal were not disclosed.

"I am pleased to be back in Cincinnati. I intend on playing a full season with the Cincinnati Reds," said Sanders, who entered the news conference walking hand-in-hand with controversial Reds owner Marge Schott.

"This is the only team ... in baseball that I have really felt like it was a family. I love the city of Cincinnati, I really do, and that had a lot to do with it," added Sanders, who also has played baseball for the New York Yankees, Atlanta Braves and San Francisco Giants.

Sanders, considered the premier defensive back in the National Football League and one of its speediest players, played both defence and offence for the Dallas Cowboys this past season after putting his baseball career on hold.
In addition to his full-time defensive chores at cornerback, Sanders played wide receiver for Dallas, making 36 catches for 475 yards.
He is the only athlete to play in both baseball's World Series and football's Super Bowl.
He was a member of the Atlanta Braves team that lost the World Series in 1992.

He won the 1995 Super Bowl following his one season with the San Francisco 49ers. He then signed a highly-publicised seven-year, $35 million contract with the Cowboys and won another Super Bowl in his first season with Dallas.
Sanders committed himself full time to football in 1996 and had been without a baseball contract since finishing the 1995 season with San Francisco Giants.
"In my life, this is a chapter that I'm not willing to close at this time, that's why I reopened it, because I truly enjoy the game of baseball," the flashy star said.
"It's all my body knows. I've been doing it since I was seven years old, playing both sports."
He said he does not expect his return to baseball to affect his status with the Cowboys.
"The Dallas Cowboys are probably the best organisation in sports, period, and I'm glad to be a part of that, and I want to be a part of that for the rest of my career," he said.
This will mark Sanders's second stint with the Reds, who traded him to the Giants in July of 1995.

In his 494-game career, Sanders is a .264 hitter with 33 homers, 141 RBI and 127 steals. He is the only player ever to lead a league in triples while playing less than 100 games, stroking 14 for the Braves in 97 contests in 1992.
"We are extremely pleased that we are able to bring Deion back to baseball and Cincinnati, where he belongs," Reds general manager Jim Bowden said.
"Deion is one of the best athletes in the world, and has always had the potential to be one of the premier leadoff hitters in the league."
